## Direct human update — 2026-10-05 15:34 UTC

Matthew explicitly raised the Calibrate human-ready queue cap from 5 to **20** and requested more parallel implementation, while preserving the human review boundary. This supersedes the earlier cap and sole-implementation-slot constraint.

Coordinator adopts an initial resource bound of **up to 3 independent implementation tasks and 1 independent QA task on MCHARTIER_ZBOOK**, shared across active ZBook work so Little Say does not silently multiply machine load. Actual dispatch remains dependency- and resource-aware; reduce concurrency if builds, browsers or databases contend. Little Say remains a separately authorized bounded batch outside the Calibrate review-queue count. One writer per branch, isolated worktrees, existing owner continuations, no duplicate running/unknown owners, independent QA and all readiness/evidence/receipt gates remain required. Twenty is queue capacity, not twenty simultaneous workers.

Matthew also requested a scoped issue to migrate Calibrate's existing user accounts/authentication to Firebase Auth. Existing accounts and their identity/data/access must be preserved. Current implementation and Firebase import/migration capabilities are being investigated before issue publication; no live account migration or provisioning is authorized by issue scoping.

The existing finite pilot schedule and hard cutoff 2026-10-17 15:53 America/Los_Angeles are unchanged. No merge, auto-merge, release, deployment, credential expansion or gate waiver is authorized. Execution pins remain workflow-v3 f0919b184b6344d6279178b2388190936ca432a9 plus pr-review-v3 97e5583c8355f3673aad0835c0ce3ca1486aeb8b and the direct focused-diff/final-state amendments; publication of guidance does not silently migrate pins.
